title: Token Pace Lab: reproducible tokens/sec benchmark harness and regression detector
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a maintainable, reproducible microbenchmark harness (Token Pace Lab) that measures tokens/sec and p95 token latency across core serving models and hardware profiles. The harness must support deterministic replay, configurable prompt archetype mixes, GPU kernel telemetry correlation, and automatic regression detection suitable for CI gating. This ticket covers the benchmark design, implementation of the runner + analysis pipeline, and integration into nightly CI with dashboarding and PR checks.
acceptance_criteria: Runner can execute stable token/sec and p95 measurements across a configurable set of models and sequence lengths with <5% run-to-run variance on identical infra
Support for 4 workload archetypes: short instruction, multi-turn chat, long-context generation, and code completion; each with tokenization-aware length distribution
Deterministic replay mode that pins RNG and synthetic prompt sampling seed to reproduce any measurement run
Automated regression detector producing pass/fail for CI PR checks using control-chart + CUSUM with smoothing and an option for EWMA fallback
Grafana dashboard with nightly golden-run baseline overlays, percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), and correlated GPU kernel utilization traces
Integration hook that posts summarized results and PR link to the originating GitHub PR; failing runs block merge if thresholds are exceeded
implementation_notes: Workload driver: lightweight Rust binary that uses existing inference client; allows parallel connections and configurable batching patterns
Prompt library: seedable generator with archetype buckets, token-length histograms and optional prefix reuse simulation (to exercise KV cache)
Telemetry: collect per-token timing, rk (KV) hit ratio, CUDA occupancy summaries, and runtime kernel names where available
Regression logic: compute normalized delta against nightly 'golden' run; use CUSUM with a 3-sigma threshold and exponential smoothing to reduce flakiness
CI: nightly baseline job stores golden-run fingerprints (signed artifact); PR job compares to latest golden and nightly median
Artifacts: results written to JSONL with deterministic run metadata (seed, infra hash, model sha/hash, driver version) for postmortem replay
Fallback: when kernel-level telemetry is unavailable (private envs), fall back to token timing + resource-level metrics (GPU util, mem)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Running full stability experiments on every PR is expensive; we balance by running quick smoke probes in PRs and nightly full-runs
CUSUM reduces false positives but introduces detection lag; to mitigate, we run both fast-detection (PR) and sensitive-detection (nightly)
Deterministic replay requires pinning underlying libraries (CUDA, runtime); we maintain infra-hash in artifacts and fail if runtime mismatch detected
updates: 2025-02-05: Spike complete. Prototype runner implemented in Rust and validated against a subset of core models. Observed ~3.8% run-to-run variance for short-instruction archetype on a fixed GPU instance.

2025-02-18: Decided on control-chart + CUSUM hybrid for regression detection after testing EWMA/EWMA+CUSUM variants (noted lower false positives with hybrid). Added deterministic seed to prompt generator.
2025-02-26: Integrated kernel telemetry collector. Need infra change request to allow /proc access for kernel names on our CI images — opened infra ticket ENG-560892 (linked).
2025-03-01: Dashboard prototype pushed (grafana/dashboards/token-pace-lab.json). Nightly job scheduled in CI; golden-run artifacts stored in s3://redwood-bench/golden/token-pace/2025-02-28.jsonl

2025-03-04: PR gating policy drafted: PRs run a 4-min smoke probe (short-instruction + low concurrency) and fail only on >15% regression in tokens/sec sustained across probes. Nightly full-run retains stricter 7% threshold and CUSUM sensitivity. Ready for UX/Docs review.
